findings.witness: Unit flat torus, slope1/10 capsule of width1/1000 around s in[-.01,1.01], simple primitive curve along s in[0,1] then vertical return; transboundary length<.611 while axis length1. Bounded geometry600; one essential intersection.

findings.title: Squared norms and weak admissibility quantifiers

per_problem.claim_location: Lemma 5.4, PDF 16–18, particularly (14) on PDF 17; Proposition 7.2 on PDF 20
per_problem.decisive_analysis: Reconstructed the capsule in the unit flat torus. Vertical span is 13/125; nontrivial vertical lattice translates are disjoint, and the only possible horizontal translates have supporting-line separation 1/sqrt(101)>2/1000. The projected closure is an embedded contractible disk, contains the radius-1/1000 ball at (1/2,1/20), and lies in a radius-3/5 ball, so the bounded-geometry constant 600 is valid. The slanted segment followed by the vertical return is simple, primitive horizontal, has exactly one essential excursion and meets one annular-cover lift. Its outside length is at most 1/10 and the lift diameter is at most sqrt(16301)/250<511/1000; the asserted unit-axis lower bound therefore fails. Lemma 5.4 does not require density or a wandering diffeomorphism, so those global requirements do not exclude this auxiliary counterexample.
per_problem.counterevidence_and_repair: A connected subset of the axis circle has H1 at most twice its circular diameter. This yields a factor two only on the discrete contributions; N/c lift comparison gives the required uniform O(length^-2) bound. In the q-metric competitor the continuous density remains |q|^(1/2), so the strict continuous-area gap survives. The theorem and the stated conclusion of Lemma 5.4 are not refuted.
per_problem.impact: The false estimate is explicitly used in both proof branches; retaining Major follows the agreed core-derivation criterion despite the local repair.

per_problem.claim_location: Definition (7) on PDF 7, Hilbert norm/mass on PDF 8, Lemma 7.3 on PDF 20–21
per_problem.decisive_analysis: The source defines mass as squared norm and admissibility outside a family of classical 2-modulus zero, so the printed unsquared equalities and every-height assertion do not follow. A single horizontal circle has modulus zero. For circumference one, the family indexed by a measurable height set E has modulus |E| by Cauchy–Schwarz and the cylinder density; arbitrary exceptional height sets are covered using small-energy admissible densities. Thus the needed inequality holds almost everywhere.
per_problem.counterevidence_and_repair: Using the explicitly accepted full-area single-curve Jenkins–Strebel cylinder, Fubini gives mass(rho0)>=area(Cq)>area_q(S)=||rho1|S||^2. The exact variation is 2t(<u,v>-||u||^2)+t^2(||v-u||^2+||d||^2), with negative first-order term and finite second-order term. This verifies the stated local repair without claiming the external cylinder theorem was reproved.
per_problem.impact: Local normalization and admissibility quantifiers; the repaired final contradiction remains valid.

per_problem.decisive_analysis: The actual page prints arccosh(coth(length)/2). Since coth(L)<2 iff L>log(3)/2, L=1 gives a nonreal width. No upper bound excluding these lengths appears in the paragraph.
per_problem.counterevidence_and_repair: A sufficiently small embedded annular neighborhood and a relatively compact conformal subannulus supply all subsequent derivative and length bounds; no numerical collar width is required.
per_problem.impact: The local choice is corrected without changing Corollary 5.2 or the main theorem.
